chunks: And Zakariyyā al-Naqqāḍ narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
"Do not approach salat (prayer) while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying."
He said: "Included in it is the intoxication of sleep."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the act of worship one must not approach in a state of impaired awareness
key_terms.النَّوْمِ: sleep; meaning drowsiness or sleep-induced impairment
key_terms.تَعْلَمُوا: you know; meaning conscious awareness of one's words in salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَقُولُونَ: you are saying; the recitations and words uttered in salat (prayer)
key_terms.سُكَارَى: intoxicated; in this context, a state in which awareness is diminished
key_terms.سُكْرُ: intoxication; here used for a condition that prevents proper awareness

ai.seo_question: Does the verse about not approaching salat (prayer) while intoxicated also apply to sleepiness?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explains that the Qur'anic prohibition on approaching salat (prayer) while intoxicated also includes the state of drowsiness and sleepiness. The meaning is that one should not stand for salat (prayer) unless aware of what one is saying.
